question: An enchantment can enter the battlefield as a copy of an artifact, 'except it's an enchantment in addition to its other types.' It enters as a copy of a plain artifact creature. If something later copies that permanent, does the new copy also pick up the extra enchantment type, or only the original artifact creature's types?
workedSolution: Copy Artifact is an enchantment that reads, “You may have this enchantment enter as a copy of any artifact on the battlefield, except it’s an enchantment in addition to its other types.” It enters the battlefield as a copy of Juggernaut. The copiable values of the Copy Artifact now match those of Juggernaut with one modification: its types are now artifact, creature, and enchantment.

whyHard: Players treat an "except" clause on a copy effect as a one-time patch applied only at that moment, not as something that sticks. In fact a copy effect's own modification becomes part of the permanent's copiable values going forward, so anything that copies that permanent afterward inherits the modification too, not just the values of the thing originally copied.
